MAJAZ:v1p14/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p14/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p14/r5.claim: The preposition في is used with the sense ‘on’ in this phrase.
MAJAZ:v1p14/r5.anchor: وقال: «لأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل» (20/ 71) معناه: على جذوع النخل

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r1.claim: The magicians' profession of faith rejects Pharaoh's divinity and directly challenges his sovereignty, not merely his religious claims.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r1.anchor: a direct impact on his divinity and sovereignty as a king

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r2.claim: Pharaoh alleges Moses trained the magicians and arranged a staged defeat, calling them conspirators to protect his rule.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r2.anchor: He has taught them the skill of magic

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r3.claim: The conspiracy story is a lame excuse after Pharaoh was defeated by forces he had assembled; his clever pretext might fool many, but cannot suppress truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r3.anchor: the truth cannot be subdued with such deceptive measures

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r4.claim: Pharaoh imposes an insurgent's punishment: severing limbs on opposite sides and public crucifixion to make an example of the magicians.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r4.anchor: their limbs were to be severed from opposite sides

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r5.claim: Crucifying them on palm trunks signals the public nature of the punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r6.claim: Pharaoh invokes the belief that a magician's disobedient disciple may suffer a calamity from his mentor, warning his own punishment would be harsher and longer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p50/r6.anchor: a great calamity from his mentor

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r1.claim: آمنتم له is read either as a question or as a statement; the author refers to the earlier discussion in al-Aʿrāf for its arguments.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بالاستفهام والإخبار وقد ذكرت علله في الأعراف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p291/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p291/r1.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p291/r1.claim: Hafs has several reported forms for ءامنتم across three places; Mujahid says the established reading is unlengthened, declarative, with no disagreement, and Warsh from Nafi agrees.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p291/r1.anchor: والمعروف عن حفص عن عاصم أن الثلاثة الأحرف بغير مد على لفظ الخبر لا خلاف بينهن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r6.claim: The author points to earlier discussion of the readings آمنتم, لأقطعن, and لأصلبن in al-Aʿraf and its treatment of the parallel verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r6.anchor: وتقدم الخلاف في قراءة آمنتم وفي لأقطعن ولأصلبن في الأعراف. وتفسير نظير هذه الآية فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r7.claim: The parallel in al-Aʿraf uses آمنتم به, while this verse has آمنتم له; آمن usually takes bi when faith is in God and li for others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r7.anchor: وجاء هناك آمنتم به وهنا له، وآمن يوصل بالباء إذا كان بالله وباللام لغيره في الأكثر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r8.claim: The cited examples of آمن taking li are فما آمن لموسى, لن نؤمن لك, وما أنت بمؤمن لنا, and فآمن له لوط.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r8.anchor: نحو فما آمن لموسى لن نؤمن لك وما أنت بمؤمن لنا فآمن له لوط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r9.claim: In the al-Aʿraf version, the pronoun in به may refer either to Moses or to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r9.anchor: واحتمل الضمير في به أن يعود على موسى وأن يعود على الرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r10.claim: Cutting hands and feet on opposite sides is mutilation; crucifixion is described with في because the trunk contains the victim, like a vessel containing its contents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r10.anchor: وأراد بالتقطيع والتصليب في الجذوع التمثيل بهم، ولما كان الجذع مقرا للمصلوب واشتمل عليه اشتمال الظرف على المظروف عدي الفعل بفي التي للوعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r11.claim: Some take في to mean على; another explanation says Pharaoh bored into the wood and put the victims inside it, literally making the trunk their container until starvation and thirst killed them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r11.anchor: وقيل في بمعنى على. وقيل: نقر فرعون الخشب وصلبهم في داخله فصار ظرفا لهم حقيقة حتى يموتوا فيه جوعا وعطشا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r12.claim: A poet’s line uses صلبوا with في to describe crucifying a man from ʿAbd in a palm trunk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r12.anchor: ومن تعدية صلب بفي قول الشاعر: وهم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r13.claim: The author says Pharaoh was the first to crucify.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r14.claim: The threat asks which is harsher and longer-lasting: Pharaoh or the one the believers accepted, with another view taking the comparison as Pharaoh versus Moses; al-Zamakhshari says Pharaoh mocks Moses as no torturer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358/r14.anchor: وهو ولتعلمن أينا أي أبي وأي من آمنتم به. وقيل: أبي وأي موسى، وقال ذلك على سبيل الاستهزاء لأن موسى لم يكن من أهل التعذيب

TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r7.claim: Cutting hands and feet crosswise means cutting the right hand and left foot; crucifixion is intensified or multiplied, and the trunks are palm trunks.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r7.anchor: وقطع الأيدي والأرجل من خلاف أن يقطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى والتصليب تكثير الصلب وتشديده

TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r8.claim: Pharaoh's question about their believing before permission may be an interrogative with an omitted particle expressing denial, or a declarative sentence meant to establish their alleged crime.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r8.anchor: والجملة استفهامية محذوفة الأداة والاستفهام للإنكار أو خبرية مسوقة لتقرير الجرم

TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r9.claim: Pharaoh accuses the magicians of a political pact with Moses to stage his prophecy, gather Egyptians and the magicians, then feign defeat so the crowd follows and the established order is removed.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#10/r9.anchor: كأنهم تواطؤوا مع رئيسهم أن يتنبأ موسى فيدعو أهل مصر إلى الله ويأتي في ذلك بسحر

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r1.claim: Pharaoh repeats the charge elsewhere as a plot in the city to expel its people; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the accusation was meant to incite the public against the magicians, as Pharaoh had incited them against Moses earlier.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r1.anchor: إنما رماهم بهذا القول تهييجا للعامة عليهم كما رمى موسى عليه السلام بمثله في أول يوم

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r2.claim: The Qur'an records Pharaoh's threat of severe punishment but does not state whether he actually carried it out.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r2.anchor: ولم يذكر تعالى في كلامه أنجز فيهم ذلك أم لا؟

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r6.claim: Pharaoh is oblivious to God, sees only himself as Egypt's lord with subjects, land, and armies, and imagines truth must submit to his falsehood and people's recognition of truth must await his permission.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r6.anchor: يرى أن الحق تبع باطله والحقيقة خاضعة مطيعة لدعواه فيتوقع أن لا تمس نفوس الناس

TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r7.claim: Pharaoh treats the physical body and its decay as the only human reality and material pleasures as the only happiness, as shown by his threat of bodily torture.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#11/r7.anchor: ويرى أن لا حقيقة للإنسان إلا هذه البنية الجسمانية التي تعيش ثم تفسد وتفنى وأن لا سعادة له إلا نيل هذه اللذائذ المادية الفانية

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r3.claim: Pharaoh's first insinuation was that immediate belief without investigation, debate, or deliberation could not be considered insight-based and must have another cause.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r3.anchor: الاعتماد على الخاطر الأول غير جائز بل لا بد فيه من البحث والمناظرة والاستعانة بالخواطر

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r4.claim: Pharaoh's second insinuation was that the magicians were Moses' pupils and had agreed to feign defeat to promote and glorify him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r4.anchor: يعني أنكم تلامذته في السحر فاصطلحتم على أن تظهروا العجز من أنفسكم ترويجا لأمره وتفخيما لشأنه

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r5.claim: After casting doubt on them, Pharaoh threatened them to deter them and to discourage others from following their example of belief.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r5.anchor: ثم بعد إيراد الشبهة اشتغل بالتهديد تنفيرا لهم عن الإيمان وتنفيرا لغيرهم عن الاقتداء بهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r6.claim: Rāzī notes an unnamed reading that lightens the forms of both “I will cut off” and “I will crucify.”

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r7.claim: Cutting crosswise means cutting the right hand and left foot, since each is opposite the other in limb and side.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r7.anchor: والقطع من خلاف أن تقطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى لأن كل واحد من العضوين خلاف الآخر

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r8.claim: “Crosswise” is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier: the limbs are to be cut in differing ways.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r8.anchor: في محل النصب على الحال أي

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r9.claim: The preposition “in” depicts the crucified person as lodged in a trunk like something enclosed in its container; the popular gloss “on the trunks” is weak.

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r10.claim: By “which of us,” Pharaoh meant himself and Moses, boasting of his power and habitual cruelty while mocking Moses, who had never tortured anyone.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r10.anchor: يشعر بأنه أراد نفسه وموسى عليه السلام بدليل

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r11.claim: Although Pharaoh had recently seen the staff become a terrifying serpent and sought Moses' help, Rāzī says Pharaoh may have been inwardly terrified while feigning boldness to preserve his rule; helpless people sometimes act this way.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r11.anchor: قلنا لم لا يجوز أن يقال : إنه كان في أشد الخوف في قلبه

RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r12.claim: Rāzī cites Pharaoh's denial that God's punishment exceeds human punishment and his knowingly false claim about Moses teaching the magicians as evidence of calculated public bravado.
RAZI-FULL:v22p76/r12.anchor: ومما يدل على صحة ذلك أن كل عاقل يعلم بالضرورة

STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.claim: The passage is cross-referenced with 7:123–26 and, for verse 71, 26:49.
STUDYQURAN:20:71/r3.anchor: See commentary on 7:123–26; cf. also v. 71 with 26:49

TAB-FULL:v16p113/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r3.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r3.claim: In Saʿid’s account, Pharaoh was the first to cut off hands and feet crosswise and to crucify people on palm trunks.
TAB-FULL:v16p113/r3.anchor: قال: فكان أول من قطع الأيدي والأرجل من خلاف فرعون {ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل} [طه: 71] قال: فكان أول من صلب في جذوع النخل فرعون

TAB-FULL:v16p114/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p114/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p114/r1.claim: Wahb says Pharaoh angrily saw he had been overcome when the magicians believed; al-Tabari explains his accusation as asking whether they had affirmed Moses before permission, and calls Moses their chief and greatest sorcerer who taught them.
TAB-FULL:v16p114/r1.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، قال: لما قالت السحرة

TAB-FULL:v16p116/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r1.claim: Al-Tabari explains crosswise cutting as removing opposite hands and feet and says Pharaoh was the first to do it; al-Suddi reports that Pharaoh killed and cut the magicians after his threat.

TAB-FULL:v16p116/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r2.claim: Here في means ‘on’ the palm trunks; the condemned person was stretched along the tree, so Arabic describes him as crucified in it. The cited verse uses the phrase with a trunk as support.
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r2.anchor: يقول: ولأصلبنكم على جذوع النخل، كما قال الشاعر

TAB-FULL:v16p116/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r3.claim: Qatada says the magicians recognized the sign as from God and prostrated; Pharaoh then threatened them with crosswise amputation and crucifixion.
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل}

TAB-FULL:v16p116/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says they began the day as magicians and ended it as martyrs after praying for patience and to die as Muslims.
TAB-FULL:v16p116/r4.anchor: كما قال عبد الله بن عباس حين قالوا: {ربنا أفرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين} [الأعراف: 126] وقال: كانوا في أول النهار سحرة، وفي آخر النهار شهداء

TABRISI:20:71/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r7.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:20:71/r7.claim: Al-Kisa'i says people in the Hijaz call a teacher كبير; in Arabic كبير means a leader or chief.
TABRISI:20:71/r7.anchor: قال الكسائي: الصبي في الحجاز إذا جاء

TABRISI:20:71/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71/r8.claim: الإيثار means choosing; تزكي means seeking growth or purification, and zakat is so named because wealth grows through it.

TABRISI:20:71/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71/r10.claim: آمنتم به uses the preposition باء for faith as the opposite of disbelief, while آمنتم له means believing or affirming someone.
TABRISI:20:71/r10.anchor: والفرق بين آمنتم به وآمنتم له إن آمنتم به بالباء

TABRISI:20:71/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71/r11.claim: من can mean عن, yielding 'from opposite sides,' or على, yielding 'on opposite sides'; the prepositional phrase is an accusative circumstantial expression.
TABRISI:20:71/r11.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون من بمعنى عن أي عن خلاف

TABRISI:20:71/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71/r12.claim: Here في means على, 'on the palm trunks,' because the trunks surround the victims and so they are described as being inside them.
TABRISI:20:71/r12.anchor: في بمعنى على وإنما جاز ذلك لأن الجذع قد اشتمل عليهم

TABRISI:20:71-72/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r1.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses crucifixion “in” a palm trunk, illustrating the phrase about crucifixion on palm trunks.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r1.anchor: هم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة

TABRISI:20:71-72/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-72/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-72/r2.claim: The interrogative clause is suspended in meaning: the relevant verb acts semantically but not syntactically on it.
TABRISI:20:71-72/r2.anchor: { أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى } تعليق ومعنى التعليق إن عملت تعمل في المعنى

TABRISI:20:71-74/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r4.claim: Pharaoh means, “Have you believed Moses?” or “You have believed him.”
TABRISI:20:71-74/r4.anchor: آمنتم له } أي لموسى والمعنى قد صدقتم له

TABRISI:20:71-74/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r5.claim: Pharaoh means they acted without his permission; his ignorance made him think no religion could be believed without his authorization.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r5.anchor: أي من غير إذني لأنه بلغ من جهله أنه لا يعتقد دين إلا بإذنه

TABRISI:20:71-74/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r6.claim: An order indicates the commander’s will that the commanded act occur, while permission does not necessarily indicate that will.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r6.anchor: والفرق بين الإذن والأمر أن في الأمر دلالة على إرادة الآمر الفعل المأمور به

TABRISI:20:71-74/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r7.claim: فاصطادوا in 5:2 is an example of permission; أقيموا الصلاة in 6:72 is an order.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r7.anchor:
فإذا حللتم فاصطادوا
[المائدة: 2] إذن وقوله
أقيموا الصلاة
[الأنعام: 72] أمر

TABRISI:20:71-74/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r8.claim: One interpretation is that Moses was their teacher and they his pupils, who might be unable to match their teacher.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r8.anchor: معناه أنه لأستاذكم وأنتم تلامذته وقد يعجز التلميذ عما يفعله الأستاذ

TABRISI:20:71-74/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r9.claim: Alternatively, Moses was their chief and they his followers; they could have opposed him but refrained out of respect.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r9.anchor: وقيل: إنه لرئيسكم ومتقدمكم وأنتم أشياعه وأتباعه ما عجزتم عن معارضته

TABRISI:20:71-74/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r10.claim: Pharaoh said this to make common people think the magicians coordinated with Moses and to turn the crowd toward them.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r10.anchor: ليوهم العوام أن ما أتوا به إنما هو لتواطؤ من جهتهم ليصرفوا وجوه الناس إليهم

TABRISI:20:71-74/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r11.claim: Cutting hands and feet “from opposite sides” means the right hands and left feet.

TABRISI:20:71-74/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r12.claim: The phrase means crucifying them on the trunks of palm trees.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r12.anchor: أي على جذوع النخل { ولتعلمن } أيها السحرة

TABRISI:20:71-74/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r13.claim: Pharaoh asks whether he, for their belief in him, or Moses’ Lord, for their rejection of Him, will punish them more severely and longer.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r13.anchor: أنا على إيمانكم أم رب موسى على ترككم الإيمان به

THALABI:v6p253/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p253/r1.claim: A poetic citation uses the image of crucifying someone on a palm trunk, echoing Pharaoh's threat to crucify the magicians.
THALABI:v6p253/r1.anchor: وهم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r1.claim: The discussion of the readings of āmantum was given earlier in the commentary on al-Aʿrāf.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r2.claim: The source distinguishes prepositions: bi is used for belief in God, while li is used for belief in another, as simple assent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r2.anchor: بوصل الباء إذا كان بالله تعالى، وإذا كان بغيره وصل باللام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r3.claim: The prepositional forms are compared with examples in 10:83, 17:90, 12:17, and 29:26; 7:123 uses bi with the same meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r3.anchor: مثل قوله: {فما آمن لموسى} [يونس: 83]، {وقالوا لن نؤمن لك} [الإسراء: 90]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains kabīr as the magicians’ teacher; Meccan usage also calls a teacher “my kabīr.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r5.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says a child in the Hijaz says “I came from my kabīr” when returning from a teacher.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r5.anchor: وقال الكسائي: (الصبي بالحجاز إذا جاء من عند معلمه قال: جئت من عند كبيري)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq reads the phrase as “the greatest of the magicians.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: (إنه لعظيم السحار)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r7.claim: In Arabic, kabīr means leader, not eldest; Joseph 12:80 calls the most knowledgeable among them their leader, hence a teacher can be called kabīr.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r8.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r8.claim: The People of Meanings say Pharaoh portrayed the magicians’ prostration as proof they followed their chief, to turn people away from Moses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p463/r8.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: جعل نسبتهم إلى اتباع رئيسهم بالسجود علة لصرف الناس عن اتباع موسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r1.speaker: المبرد، أبو عبيدة، الفراء، الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r1.claim: They explain fī as “on”: the trunks enclose the crucified men and become their place, like a house; two cited poems use this placement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r1.anchor: قال المبرد: (المعنى على جذوع النخل، وإنما وقعت في ومعانيها الوعاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r2.speaker: الأسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r2.claim: Al-Asadī’s line says graves were set above the trunks, illustrating the placement sense of fī.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r2.anchor: قال الأسدي (¬4): تداركت شماسا ويحيى وخالدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r3.claim: A second cited line says the al-ʿAbdī was crucified in a palm trunk; the surrounding authorities use it to illustrate the enclosure sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r3.anchor: وأنشدوا (¬6): وهم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p464/r4.claim: Pharaoh says the magicians will learn who inflicts harsher and longer-lasting punishment: he for their belief, or the Lord of Moses for their refusal to believe.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r1.claim: Pharaoh accuses the magicians of believing Moses before receiving his permission.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r1.anchor: صدقتموه { قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r2.claim: Pharaoh alleges that Moses is their chief and teacher of magic.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r3.claim: Their limbs will be cut crosswise: the right hand and left foot.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r4.claim: They will be crucified on the tops of palm trees.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r5.claim: Pharaoh threatens that they will learn whether he or the Lord of Moses gives the more severe and lasting punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:71-73/r5.anchor: أنا أو رب موسى { وأبقى } وأدوم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh is the speaker who challenges them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r2.anchor: فألقي السحرة سجدا قالوا آمنا برب هارون وموسى {70} قال} [طه: 70-71] فرعون.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r3.claim: Pharaoh asks whether they really believed Moses.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r3.anchor: {آمنتم له} [طه: 71] فرعون يقوله على الاستفهام، أصدقتموه؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r4.claim: His phrase means that they had already gone ahead and done it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r4.anchor: قبل أن آذن لكم} [طه: 71] أي: قد فعلتم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r5.claim: Pharaoh accuses Moses of being their chief in sorcery.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r6.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says Pharaoh means Moses is the most learned in sorcery, not the oldest.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r6.anchor: وقال السدي: يعني لعالمكم في علم السحر، ولم يكن أكبرهم في السن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r7.claim: The cutting is of the right hand and left foot.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r7.anchor: من خلاف} [طه: 71] اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r8.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddī interprets crucifying them in the trunks as on the trunks of the palms.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r8.anchor: يعني: على جذوع النخل. وهو تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r9.claim: The contest over whose punishment is harsher and more lasting is between Pharaoh and Moses.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p266#2/r9.anchor: ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا وأبقى} [طه: 71] أنا أو موسى.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.claim: Israelite presence in Egypt and Moses' effort to lead them back to their homeland created political anxiety for Pharaoh's government and a psychological warfare setting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.anchor: İsrâiloğulları’nın Mısır’daki varlığının ve Hz. Mûsâ tarafından eski yurtlarına götürülmeleri için ortaya konan çabanın Firavun yönetimi nezdinde oluşturduğu siyasî kaygılar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r6.claim: Pharaoh responded by threatening the believing magicians with severe punishment and torture.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r6.anchor: Firavun bununla da yetinmeyip iman eden sihirbazları çok ağır ceza ve işkencelerle tehdit etme yoluna girdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r7.claim: After tasting faith, the magicians recognized that no worldly reward, even being spared, could compare with the happiness of the afterlife and dared to say so openly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r7.anchor: idrak edip bunu açıkça ifade etme cesaretini gösterdiler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.claim: The commentary points readers to compare the Qur'anic account with the Biblical account of the episode.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.anchor: bu olayla ilgili bilgilerin Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’tekilerle karşılaştırılması için bk. A‘râf 7/103-126

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r6.claim: Pharaoh answered their conversion with threats of killing, crosswise amputation, crucifixion, and severe punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r6.anchor: وتوعدهم بالقتل والصلب ، وفنون من العذاب الصعب

QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r7.claim: The magicians moved from swearing by Pharaoh's might to swearing by God, becoming believers and righteous within a single day.
QUSHAYRI:v2p266/r7.anchor: وبعدما كانوا يقسمون بعزة فرعون صاروا يحلفون بالله

BURHAN:v4p302/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r6.claim: One view treats في as containment because a trunk is like a grave for the crucified; another says في suggests ease, since على implies upward movement.
BURHAN:v4p302/r6.anchor: وقيل ظرفية لأن الجذع للمصلوب بمنزلة القبر للمقبور

BURHAN:v4p302/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r7.claim: Another explanation says في was chosen to suggest their crucifixion would be easy, since على suggests having to move upward.
BURHAN:v4p302/r7.anchor: وقيل إنما آثر لفظة في للإشعار بسهولة صلبهم

BURHAN:v4p176/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p176/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p176/r2.claim: ‘Fī’ is more exact than ‘ʿalā’: the condemned are crucified in the trunks’ middles, whereas ‘ʿalā’ suggests being on top.
BURHAN:v4p176/r2.anchor: ولم يقل على كما ظن بعضهم لأن على للاستعلاء والمصلوب لا يجعل على رءوس النخل

DAMGHANI:v1p365/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r9.claim: Fī can mean 'on': Pharaoh threatens to crucify people on palm trunks.
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r9.anchor: في بمعنى على قوله تعالى في سورة طه ولاصلبنكم في جذوع النخل يعني على

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r5.claim: The third use means ʿalā, as in spending upon the garden and crucifying upon palm trunks.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p475/r5.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى ' على ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف :

FARRA:v2p186/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p186/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p186/r2.claim: In a phrase like this, the prepositions عن, على, and باء can also be used.
FARRA:v2p186/r2.anchor: ويصلح في مثله من الكلام عن وعلى والباء.

FARRA:v2p186/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p186/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p186/r3.claim: على can replace في: في suits the body raised along the trunk, while على suits its being elevated onto it; similarly, على ملك سليمان means in Solomon's kingdom.
FARRA:v2p186/r3.anchor: يصلح (على) في موضع (في) وإنما صلحت (في) لأنه يرفع في الخشبة في طولها

FARRA:v2p186/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p186/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p186/r4.claim: أبقى means more lasting or enduring.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r1.claim: In ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل, في is used for على: they will crucify people on the palm trunks.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r2.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r2.claim: The poet’s line about crucifying al-ʿAbdī في جذع نخلة uses في to mean on a palm trunk.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر : وهم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r3.speaker: عنترة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r3.claim: ʿAntara says a hero’s clothes are في a tree, meaning on it because of his height.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p298/r3.anchor: وقال عنترة : بطل كأن ثيابه في سرحة

MAJAZ:v2p23/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p23/r1.speaker: بعض المكيين
MAJAZ:v2p23/r1.claim: Kabīrukum means your teacher or master; Abū ʿUbaydah reports hearing Meccans call a boy’s employer kabīrī.
MAJAZ:v2p23/r1.anchor: «لكبيركم» (71) أي معلمكم قال أبو عبيدة سمعت بعض المكيين (قال) يقول: الغلام لمستأجره كبيرى..

MAJAZ:v2p23/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p23/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p23/r2.claim: Fī here means ʿalā, “on” the palm trunks; the cited poem uses the same construction.
MAJAZ:v2p23/r2.anchor: «في جذوع النخل» (71) أي على جذوع النخل، قال: هم صلبوا العبدى فى جذع نخلة

NAHHAS:v3p48/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p48/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p48/r18.claim: The pronoun refers to Moses; Pharaoh falsely tells the crowd that Moses is their superior in magic and arranged this display by teaching them.
NAHHAS:v3p48/r18.anchor: الضمير عائد على موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم احتال فرعون في التشبيه على الناس بهذا

NAHHAS:v3p48/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p48/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p48/r19.claim: Pharaoh carried out his threat, cutting their opposite limbs and crucifying them until they died.
NAHHAS:v3p48/r19.anchor: فقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف وصلبهم حتى ماتوا

NAHHAS:v3p48/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p48/r20.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p48/r20.claim: Abu Ishaq says أينا is nominative because its interrogative form prevents the preceding report from governing it.
NAHHAS:v3p48/r20.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق رفعت أيا لأن لفظها لفظ الاستفهام فلم يعمل فيها ما قبلها لأنه خبر

SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r1.claim: من خلاف is circumstantial, meaning limbs on opposite sides; من marks the starting point.
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r1.anchor: و " من خلاف " حال أي: مختلفة. و " من " لابتداء الغاية،

SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r2.claim: A literal account says Pharaoh hollowed palm trunks, placed the magicians inside, and left them to die of hunger and thirst.
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r2.anchor: قوله: { في جذوع النخل } يحتمل أن يكون حقيقة، وفي التفسير: أنه نقر جذوع النخل حتى جوفها، ووضعهم فيها، فماتوا جوعا وعطشا،

SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r3.claim: Figuratively, في may replace على; an anonymous verse illustrates clothing located in a tree.
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r3.anchor: والأصل: على جذوع النخل كقول الآخر:

SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r4.claim: Another figurative account compares their firm placement to people enclosed and enveloped by a trunk.
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r4.anchor: والثاني: أنه شبه تمكنهم بتمكن من حواه الجذع واشتمل عليه.

SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r5.claim: The author cites an anonymous poem using صلب with في as a construction for crucifixion in a palm trunk.
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r5.anchor: ومن تعدي " صلب " ب " في " قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r6.claim: أينا أشد is subject plus predicate; the clause fills both objects of علم if it means 'know,' or one if it means 'recognize.'

SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r7.claim: If علم means recognition, أينا may be a relative meaning 'which of us,' built because it is added; its relative clause has an omitted beginning and is the object of علم.
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r7.anchor: ويجوز على جعلها عرفانية أن تكون " أينا " موصولة بمعنى الذي، وبنيت لأنه قد أضيفت، وحذف صدر صلتها،

SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r8.claim: The relative analysis is paralleled at 19:69, one analysis of ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن.
SAMIN-DURR:20:71/r8.anchor: كقوله تعالى: ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن

ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r4.claim: Fī means on the palm trunks; it is also apt because the condemned would be lengthwise along and enclosed by the trunk.
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r4.anchor: (ولأصلبنكم في جذوع) معناه على جذوع النخل

ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r5.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r5.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's line uses fī jadʿi nakhlah for being fixed on a palm trunk, illustrating the preposition's sense.
ZAJJAJ:v3p367#2/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر: وهم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة

ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p368/r1.claim: Ayyunā is nominative because it stands as an interrogative; the preceding declarative clause cannot govern it.

ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n52/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n52/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n52/r1.claim: The “him” in Pharaoh's accusation refers to Moses.

ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n53/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n53/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n53/r1.claim: Asad says Pharaoh's verb forms convey the stress on carrying out the mutilations and crucifixions in great numbers.
ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n53/r1.anchor: Regarding the meaning of the stress on "great numbers", forthcoming from the grammatical form of the verbs employed by Pharaoh

ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n54/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n54/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n54/r1.claim: The implied comparison is between Pharaoh and the God in whom the magicians now believe.
ASAD-NOTES:20:71#n54/r1.anchor: Sc., "I or the God in whom you now believe".

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r1.claim: Across Quranic usage, baqā opposes perishing and denotes enduring good and what lasts with God, including the lasting provision promised in 20:131.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r1.anchor: القرآن نقيض النفاد والفناء، فيما يبقى عند الله من عمل صالح، وما عند الله خير وأبقى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r2.speaker: قتادة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r2.claim: Qatada glosses ghābirat in the story of Lot as remaining in God’s punishment, that is, surviving or staying behind.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: غبرتْ في عذاب الله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r3.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains the phrase ‘among the ghābirīn’ as remaining into old age.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r3.anchor: وأبو عيبدة يذهب إلى أن المعنى: من الباقين في الهرم، أي بقيت حتى هرمت

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r4.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r4.claim: Al-Raghib derives the surviving sense of ghābir from the image of dust left behind by someone running.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r5.claim: The author prefers deriving ghābir from ghubra as a remainder, like residue in an udder or dust left after a cloud of dust rises.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم وورش عن نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Hafs from Asim, and Warsh from Nafi read āmantum as a statement.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير، وحفص عن عاصم، وورش عن نافع: آمنتم [طه/ 71] على لفظ الخبر.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r2.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read with an interrogative hamza followed by a lengthened vowel.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر: آمنتم بهمزة ممدودة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r3.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Abu Bakr from Asim read two hamzas, the second lengthened.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم: (أآمنتم) بهمزتين، الثانية ممدودة .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r4.claim: The statement reading rebukes the magicians for believing before Pharaoh’s permission; the question reading conveys the same rebuke and censure.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: الخبر هاهنا وجهه حسن، كأن يقرعهم على تقدمهم بين يديه، وعلى استبدادهم على ما كان منهم من الإيمان

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r5.claim: Abu Amr normally inserts an alif between two hamzas, but avoids it here because the interrogative, pattern hamza, and root alif would create an unwieldy sequence; Hamza and al-Kisaʾi retain their regular form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p237#3/r5.anchor: وأبو عمرو إذا اجتمع هذا النحو من الهمزتين أدخل بينهما ألفا، وكأنه ترك هنا هذا الأصل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم وورش عن نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r4.claim: These readers pronounce ءامنتم as a statement, not a question.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم / ءامنتم / على لفظ الخبر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r5.claim: These readers lengthen hamza as an interrogative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر / ءاامنتم / بهمزة ممدودة استفهام

IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r6.claim: These readers use two hamzas, lengthening the second, with the first interrogative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائى وأبو بكر عن عاصم / ءآمنتم / بهمزتين الثانية ممدودة والأولى للاستفهام

NASHR:v1p456/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p456/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p456/r5.claim: Against al-Dani’s view that the waw is extra in several spellings, the author argues that the alif is extra and waw represents the hamza, written to signal connected-form easing.
NASHR:v1p456/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن الزائد في ذلك هو الألف، وأن صورة الهمزة هو الواو، كتبت على مراد الوصل تنبيها على التخفيف

QIRAAT-ER:20:71:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:71:2#1/r1.speaker: Ḥamza and others
QIRAAT-ER:20:71:2#1/r1.claim: An explicit interrogative hamza turns the declaration into Pharaoh's incredulous question and makes his outrage directly rhetorical.
QIRAAT-ER:20:71:2#1/r1.anchor: Interrogative hamza prefix — transforms declarative ""you believed"" into incredulous question ""did you believe?""

QIRAAT-ER:20:71:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:71:2#2/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:20:71:2#2/r1.claim: The second hamza is softened through tashīl, creating a smoother transition while retaining the interrogative force.
QIRAAT-ER:20:71:2#2/r1.anchor: Variant hamza realization — different orthographic/phonetic treatment of the interrogative hamza; tashīl (softening) of second hamza

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r1.claim: Pharaoh asks the sorcerers whether they believed in Moses, the apparent referent of the pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r1.anchor: قال ( أي فرعون للسحرة ( آمنتم له

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r2.claim: Iman was originally transitive directly, then commonly took bi through the sense of affirmation; here li signals submission, as in انقاد له.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r2.anchor: والإيمان في الأصل متعد بنفسه ثم شاع متعدية بالباء لما فيه من التصديق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r3.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r3.claim: Al-Baḥr says iman most often takes bi when its object is God and li when its object is someone else, citing Qur'anic examples.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r3.anchor: وفي البحر إن آمن يوصل بالباء إذا كان متعلقه الله عز اسمه وباللام إن كان متعلقه غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r4.claim: He rejects the reported sense of following: the verb takes a direct object in اتبعه, not اتبع له.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r4.anchor: لا الأتباع كما قيل : لأنه متعد بنفسه يقال : اتبعه ولا يقال : اتبع له

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r5.claim: Some construe li causally: they believed in God because of Moses and the signs they witnessed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r5.anchor: وجوز أن تكون اللام تعليلية والتقدير آمنتم بالله تعالى لأجل موسى وما شاهدتم منه واختاره بعضهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r6.claim: Another view takes the pronoun in له to refer to God, though al-Alusi sees an obvious discontinuity in that reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r6.anchor: وقيل : يحتمل أن يكون ضمير له للرب عز وجل وفي الآية حينئذ تفكيك ظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r7.speaker: الأكثر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r7.claim: Most readers use the interrogative form; the rebuke is intended even on the non-interrogative reading, rather than a bare report.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأكثر ( أ آمنتم ) على الاستفهام التوبيخي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r8.claim: Pharaoh means they believed without his permission; the wording does not imply that permission would come later.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r8.anchor: أي من غير إذني لكم في الأيمان كما في قوله تعالى : ( لنفد البحر قبل أن تنفد كلمات ربي )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r9.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarsī distinguishes permission from command: command entails the commander's willing the act, while permission does not.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r9.anchor: فرق الطبرسي بين الإذن والأمر بأن الأمر يدل على إرادة الآمر الفعل المأمور به وليس في الإذن ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r10.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses their master and most knowledgeable expert in their craft, accusing him of teaching them magic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r10.anchor: لعظيمكم في فنكم وأعلمكم به وأستاذكم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r11.claim: Pharaoh first invalidates their faith as unauthorized, then says Moses taught them or coordinated the feat, answering why permission would matter after their display.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r11.anchor: ليرى قومه أن إيمانهم غير معتد به حيث كان بغير إذنه ثم استشعر أن يقولوا : أي حاجة إلى الإذن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r12.claim: His accusation was driven by fear that people would follow the sorcerers in believing Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r12.anchor: قال ذلك لما اعتراه من الخوف من اقتداء الناس بالسحرة في الإيمان لموسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r13.speaker: عامة المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r13.claim: The standard explanation is amputation of the right hand and left foot; this specification comes from external explanation, since the wording itself permits other possibilities.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r13.anchor: أي اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى وعليه عامة المفسرين وهو تخصيص من خارج

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r14.claim: Al-khilāf means the opposing side or direction, and min is partitive or originative here.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r14.anchor: والمراد من الخلاف الجانب المخالف أو الجهة المخالفة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r15.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r15.claim: Al-Ṭabarsī takes min as عن or على, but al-Alusi rejects those prepositional senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r15.anchor: وقال الطبرسي : بمعنى عن أو على

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r16.claim: Other parses attach the phrase to an omitted verbal noun meaning cutting begun on an opposite side, or treat it as circumstantial, meaning the limbs are cut on different sides.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r16.anchor: وقيل : متعلق بمحذوف وقع صفة مصدر محذوف أي تقطيع مبتدأ من جانب مخالف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r17.claim: Specifying the crosswise method conveys a definite, assured threat; it was chosen over cutting matching sides, which would kill and remove the victims' usefulness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r17.anchor: قيل للإيذان بتحقيق الأمر وإيقاعه لا محالة بتعيين كيفيته المعهودة في باب السياسة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r18.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r18.claim: Some claim crosswise amputation is the more dreadful method.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r18.anchor: فيه إهلاكا وتفويتا للمنفعة وزعم بعضهم أنها أفظع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r19.claim: Fi means on the trunks; it figuratively depicts prolonged confinement there as a container holding its contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r19.anchor: أي عليها وإيثار كلمة في للدلالة على إبقائهم عليها زمانا مديدا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r20.claim: A literal reading says Pharaoh hollowed the trunks and crucified them inside to make them die of hunger and thirst; al-Alusi considers it scarcely credible.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r20.anchor: فرعون نقر جذوع النخل وصلبهم في داخلها ليموتوا جوعا وعطشا ولا يكاد يصح

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r21.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r21.claim: Some say Pharaoh carried out the threat and was the first to crucify people; al-Razi says reports do not establish this, and al-Alusi finds the apparent account unobjectionable.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r21.anchor: فقال بعضهم : إنه أنفذ فيهم وعيده وصلبهم وهو أول من صلب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r22.claim: The threat's doubled verb forms intensify the action; victory in 28:35 can mean victory by proof rather than escape from punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r22.anchor: ولا ينافيه قوله تعالى : ( أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون ) لأن المراد الغلبة بالحجة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r23.speaker: قرئ
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r23.claim: Both verbs are also read in the lighter form.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p231/r23.anchor: وصيغة التفعيل في الفعلين للتكثير وقرئ بالتخفيف فيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r1.speaker: الطبري وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others take the comparison to be between Pharaoh and Moses, as the earlier pronoun apparently indicates.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r1.anchor: واختار ذلك الطبري وجماعة وهذا إما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r2.claim: On that reading, Pharaoh either mocks Moses as no torturer or claims the sorcerers believed from fear of Moses after seeing the staff attack their ropes and sticks.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r2.anchor: وإما لأن إيمانهم لم يكن بزعمه عن مشاهدة المعجزة ومعاينة البرهان بل كان عن خوف من قبله عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan instead takes the unstated other party to be the Lord of Moses, whom they professed to believe in as Lord of Aaron and Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r3.anchor: واختار أبو حيان أن المراد من الغير الذي أشار إليه الضمير رب موسى عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r4.claim: The verb يعلم is suspended by the interrogative clause; that clause fills two object slots if يعلم means know, or one if it means recognize.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r4.anchor: ( ولتعلمن ) هنا معلق و ( أينا أشد ) جملة استفهامية من مبتدأ وخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r5.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r5.claim: On the recognize reading, أينا may be the object, built according to Sībawayh, with أشد as the predicate of an omitted subject and its clause a relative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r5.anchor: وهو مبني على رأي سيبويه و ( أشد ) خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r6.claim: عذابا is a tamyiz; al-Alusi says that it is also understood with أبقى.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r6.anchor: وهو مراد أيضا واشتقاق أبقى من البقاء بمعنى الدوام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r7.claim: The normal derivation of أبقى is from baqāʾ meaning permanence.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r7.anchor: واشتقاق أبقى من البقاء بمعنى الدوام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r8.claim: A remote alternative derives أبقى from gifts, since Pharaoh gave gifts to those he favored; al-Alusi calls this far-fetched and compares Nimrod's boast.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r8.anchor: وقيل : لا يبعد والله تعالى أعلم أن يكون من البقاء بمعنى العطاء فإن اللعين كان يعطي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r9.claim: Pharaoh's brazen threat came just after the staff became a serpent and produced terrifying effects, even pursuing his pavilion until he sought Moses' help.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p232/r9.anchor: مع قرب عهده بما شاهد من انقلاب العصا حية وما لها من الآثار الهائلة حتى أنها قصدت ابتلاع قبته فاستغاث بموسى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r10.claim: Pharaoh accuses Moses of being the magicians' chief and teacher.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r11.claim: Pharaoh threatens to cut off their right hands and left feet or vice versa.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r11.anchor: ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل} أي: على جذوع النخل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r12.claim: Crucifying them in palm trunks means crucifying them on the trunks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r12.anchor: ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل} أي: على جذوع النخل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r13.claim: Pharaoh asks whether his punishment for their faith or Moses' Lord's punishment for rejecting faith is harsher and more lasting; abqā means more enduring.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p284/r13.anchor: {ولتعلمن أينا أشد عذابا} ؛ أنا على إيمانكم به، أو رب موسى على ترك الإيمان به؟ {وأبقى} أي: أدوم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to Moses, and the lām appears because the verb implies following him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r1.anchor: أي لموسى واللام لتضمن الفعل معنى الاتباع

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r2.speaker: قنبل وحفص
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r2.claim: Qunbul and Ḥafṣ read the words as a statement; the other readers make them a question.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r2.anchor: وقرأ قنبل وحفص { آمنتم له } على الخبر

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r3.claim: Pharaoh accuses Moses of being the magicians' master, greatest in their art, or most knowledgeable in it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r3.anchor: لعظيمكم في فنكم وأعلمكم به أو لأستاذكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r4.claim: Cutting them crosswise means the right hand and left foot; مِن marks the starting point, and the phrase is an accusative circumstantial description of differently paired limbs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r4.anchor: اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى، ومن ابتدائية

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r5.claim: Both verbs are also read with light consonants.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r6.claim: The wording compares the crucified person's firm attachment to the trunk with something held inside its container; Pharaoh was the first to crucify people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r6.anchor: شبه تمكن المصلوب بالجذع بتمكن المظروف بالظرف

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r7.claim: Pharaoh means himself and Moses, as indicated by his saying آمنتم له; the lām with belief in scripture for someone other than God belittles Moses, though Moses did not inflict punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r7.anchor: يريد نفسه وموسى لقوله { آمنتم له } واللام مع الإيمان في كتاب الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r8.claim: An alternative takes the comparison to be with the Lord of Moses, whom the magicians believed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r8.anchor: وقيل رب موسى الذي آمنوا به

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:71/r9.claim: أبقى means more enduring in punishment.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r13.claim: Pharaoh means that the magicians believed in God by following or affirming Moses.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r13.anchor: أي بالله { له } أي مصدقين أو متبعين لموسى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r14.claim: By stressing that they acted before his permission, Pharaoh insinuates that he might allow it later, keeping the crowd from following through fear and hope of permission.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r14.anchor: إبهاما بأنه سيأذن فيه ليقف الناس عن المبادرة إلى الاتباع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r15.claim: Pharaoh invents a prior conspiracy in which Moses was their magic teacher and leader, to stop his followers from accepting the manifest truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r15.anchor: فلم تتبعوه لظهور الحق , بل لإرادتكم شيئا من المكر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r16.claim: The crosswise punishment means cutting one hand and the opposite foot, distributed limb by limb.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r16.anchor: على سبيل التوزيع { وأرجلكم } أي من كل يدا ورجلا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r17.claim: Saying they would be crucified in the trunks depicts them as firmly enclosed there, intensifying the horror and deterring others.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r17.anchor: وعبر عن الاستعلاء بالظرف إشارة إلى تمكينهم من المصلوب فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p29#2/r18.claim: Pharaoh challenges whether his punishment or the Lord of Moses’ punishment is harsher and longer-lasting; Moses had warned that punishment befalls whoever denies and turns away.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r1.claim: Āmana lahu means faith arose for his sake, while āmana bihi means faith arose because of him; the verb normally takes a preposition in this sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r1.anchor: ويقال : آمن له ، أي حصل عنده الإيمان لأجله . كما يقال : آمن به ، أي حصل الإيمان عنده بسببه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r2.claim: Qālūn, Warsh by al-Azraq, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, and Rawḥ read with one hamza and lengthening, as an interrogative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r2.anchor: وقرأ قالون وورش من طريق الأزرق ، وابن عامر ، وأبو عمرو ، وأبو جعفر ، وروح عن يعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r3.claim: Warsh by al-Aṣbahānī, Ibn Kathīr, Ḥafṣ, and Ruways read with one hamza as a declarative rebuke.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r3.anchor: وقرأه ورش من طريق الأصفهاني ، وابن كثير ، وحفص عن عاصم ، ورويس عن يعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r4.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Abū Bakr, and Khalaf read with two hamzas, also interrogatively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r4.anchor: وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وأبو بكر عن عاصم ، وخلف بهمزتين على الاستفهام أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r5.claim: Unable to punish belief without violating debate conventions, Pharaoh invented the charge that they believed before receiving his permission and treated it as insolence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r5.anchor: ولكنه علم أن العقاب على الإيمان بموسى بعد أن فتح باب المناظرة معه نكث لأصول المناظرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r6.claim: Pharaoh pretended their haste proved prior collusion with Moses and claimed he would have permitted belief, to make the audience doubt what they had witnessed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r6.anchor: واستخلص من تسرعهم بذلك أنهم تواطؤوا مع موسى من قبل فأظهروا العجز عند مناظرته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r7.claim: This is the familiar defeated person’s feeble invented excuse, like defendants accusing judges of bribery or losing states alleging military treason.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r7.anchor: وهذه شنشنة من قديم الزمان اختلاق المغلوب بارد العذر . ومن هذا القبيل اتهام المحكوم عليهم الحاكمين بالارتشاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r8.anchor: وضمير له } عائد إلى موسى مثل ضمير { إنه لكبيركم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r9.claim: Before I permit you means before I allow you to believe in him; adhina lahu means to authorize something.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r9.anchor: ومعنى قبل أن آذن لكم } قبل أن أسوغ لكم أن تؤمنوا به . يقال : أذن له ، إذ أباح له شيئا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r10.claim: Taqṭīʿ intensifies cutting, with emphasis on the manner: the hand and foot are cut from opposite sides, alternating the limbs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r10.anchor: والتقطيع : شدة القطع . ومرجع المبالغة إلى الكيفية ، وهي ما وصفه بقوله { من خلاف }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r11.claim: The crosswise cutting was apparently the customary mark of criminals; the verse reports the practice rather than distinguishing a uniquely more painful form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p263/r11.anchor: والظاهر : أن القطع على هذه الكيفية كان شعارا لقطع المجرمين ، فيكون ذكر هذه الصفة حكاية للواقع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r1.claim: Islamic punishment for ḥirābah cuts only one limb for each offense, mercifully preserving use of the remaining limbs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r1.anchor: وأما ما جاء في الإسلام في عقوبة المحارب فإنما هو قطع عضو واحد عند كل حرابة فهو من الرحمة في العقوبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r2.claim: Min marks the starting point: cutting begins from opposite sides; the phrase is circumstantial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r2.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله { من خلاف } للابتداء ، أي يبدأ القطع من مبدأ المخالفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r3.claim: Taṣlīb intensifies crucifixion, which means binding a body to an upright piece of wood or nailing it there; the emphasis is on forceful nailing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r3.anchor: والتصليب : مبالغة في الصلب . والصلب : ربط الجسم على عود منتصب أو دقه عليه بمسامير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r4.claim: The preposition fī replaces ʿalā to portray the crucified as firmly embedded in the trunk, using a container metaphor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r4.anchor: ولذلك عدل عن حرف الاستعلاء إلى حرف الظرفية تشبيها لشدة تمكن المصلوب من الجذع بتمكن الشيء الواقع في وعائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r5.claim: Judhūʿ is the plural of judhʿ, a palm-tree trunk.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r5.anchor: والجذوع : جمع جذع بكسر الجيم وسكون الذال وهو عود النخلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r6.claim: Ayyunā asks which of two participants has the harsher punishment; taʿlamunna is suspended from taking an object because the question follows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r6.anchor: استفهام عن مشتركين في شدة التعذيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r7.claim: Pharaoh means himself and Moses’ Lord: he boasts that his punishment exceeds the torment Moses warned them of, an expression of arrogance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p264/r7.anchor: وأراد بالمشتركين نفسه ورب موسى سبحانه لأنه علم من قولهم آمنا برب هارون وموسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم وورش عن نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and Warsh from Nāfiʿ read āman tum as a declarative statement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم وورش عن نافع «آمنتم» على الخبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r5.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r5.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read with one hamza followed by a lengthened vowel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر «ءامنتم» بهمزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r6.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read the word with two hamzas.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم «أأمنتم» بهمزتين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r7.claim: Pharaoh’s remark shows a degree of softening and submission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r7.anchor: وقوله قبل أن آذن لكم مقاربة منه وبعض إذعان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r8.claim: The crosswise amputation means cutting the right hand and left foot.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r8.anchor: وقوله من خلاف يريد قطع اليد اليمنى مع الرجل اليسرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r9.claim: The construction is expansive: they are tied on the trunks, unlike someone being mounted on a horse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r9.anchor: قوله في جذوع النخل اتساع من حيث هو مربوط في الجذع وليست على حد قولك ركبت على الفرس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes ayna to mean Pharaoh comparing himself with the Lord of Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r10.anchor: وقوله أينا يريد نفسه ورب موسى عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Pharaoh means himself and Moses; Ibn Atiyya prefers his own reading as more consistent with Pharaoh’s fabrication.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p52#3/r11.anchor: وقال الطبري يريد نفسه وموسى عليه السلام والأول أذهب مع مخرفة فرعون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم وورش عن نافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Hafs from ʿAsim, and Warsh from Nafiʿ read ā-mantum lahu in the declarative form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وحفص عن عاصم وورش عن نافع آمنتم له على لفظ الخبر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r2.claim: Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿAmir read with a lengthened hamza.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر آمنتم له بهمزة ممدودة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r3.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read two hamzas, lengthening the second.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم أآمنتم له بهمزتين الثانية ممدودة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says kabīrukum means “your teacher”; al-Kisaʾi cites the Hijazi expression “I came from my teacher.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى إنه لكبيركم قال ابن عباس يريد معلمكم قال الكسائي الصبي بالحجاز إذا جاء من عند معلمه قال جئت من عند كبيري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r5.claim: The preposition fī means “on” here, as in 52:38.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r5.anchor: في بمعنى على ومثله أم لهم سلم يستمعون فيه الطور 38

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r6.claim: Pharaoh threatens that they will learn which of the two gives the harsher and more lasting punishment: Pharaoh for their faith or Moses' Lord for their unbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p306#3/r6.anchor: ولتعلمن أيها السحرة اينا أشد عذابا لكم وأبقى أي أدوم أنا على إيمانكم أو رب موسى على تركهم الايمان به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r1.claim: After witnessing the miracle and his own sorcerers publicly convert despite their defeat, Pharaoh defiantly falsifies the truth and abuses his power to threaten them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r1.anchor: حين رأى ما رأى من المعجزة الباهرة والآية العظيمة، ورأى الذين قد استنصر بهم قد آمنوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r2.claim: Pharaoh's “you believed him” means you affirmed Moses; “before I gave you permission” accuses them of acting without his order and against him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r2.anchor: وقال {آمنتم له} أي: صدقتموه {قبل أن آذن لكم} أي: وما أمرتكم بذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r3.claim: Pharaoh knowingly lies that Moses taught the sorcerers magic and that they colluded with him to deceive Pharaoh and his subjects; he makes the same accusation elsewhere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r3.anchor: وقال قولا يعلم هو والسحرة والخلق كلهم أنه بهت وكذب: {إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r4.claim: Pharaoh threatens to mutilate and kill them, then crucify them publicly as an example.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh was the first to carry out this form of punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فكان أول من فعل ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh says they claim he and his people are astray while Moses and his followers are guided, and threatens that they will learn who suffers the harsher, longer-lasting punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p304#2/r1.anchor: أي أنتم تقولون: إني وقومي على ضلالة، وأنتم مع موسى وقومه على الهدى

JISHUMI:v7p4699/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r1.claim: Īmān means assent in Arabic; in religious usage it names specified acts involving prohibitions, permissions, and invocations.
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r1.anchor: الإيمان في اللغة: التصديق، ومنه: (وما أنت بمؤمن لنا ولو كنا صادقين) وفي الشرغ: اسم لأفعال مخصوصة

JISHUMI:v7p4699/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r2.claim: Āmantum lahu conveys following the person believed; āmantum bihi can mean believing without following his summons.
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r2.anchor: والفرق بين قوله: (آمنتم له) و(آمنتم به). أن في (آمنتم له) معنى الاتباع، ولا كذلك (به)

JISHUMI:v7p4699/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r3.claim: Idhn is permission or release to act, originally notification; unlike a command, it implies neither desire for the act nor obligation.
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r3.anchor: والإذن: الإطلاق في الفعل، وأصله الإعلام، والفرق بين الإذن والأمر أن في الأمر إرادة المأمور به

JISHUMI:v7p4699/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r6.claim: Fī marks containment and ʿalā superposition, but one preposition can stand in for another, explaining fī where ʿalā might be expected.
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r6.anchor: (في) حرف ظرف و(على) للاستعلاء وكلاهما يخفضان ما بعدهما، ويستعمل (في) بمعنى (على)

JISHUMI:v7p4699/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r7.claim: The source says they crucified al-ʿAbdi on a palm trunk by binding him to it; the palm's enclosing them is like a vessel enclosing its contents.
JISHUMI:v7p4699/r7.anchor: هم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة وإنما شد به؛ لأن ضم النخل لهم كضم الوعاء لما فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r1.claim: One explanation of “your chief” is that Moses was their greatest sorcerer, highest in skill and rank.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r1.anchor: لعظيمكم ، يريد : أنه أسحرهم وأعلاهم درجة في صناعتهم .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, kabīr means teacher: Meccans called a teacher or instructor “my elder.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r2.anchor: أو لمعلمكم ، من قول أهل مكة للمعلم : أمرني كبيري

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r3.claim: A reading lightens the forms of both the threats to cut off and crucify.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r4.claim: Cutting “crosswise” means cutting the right hand and left foot, opposite limbs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r4.anchor: والقطع من خلاف : أن تقطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى ؛ لأن كل واحد من العضوين خالف الآخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r5.claim: Min marks the starting point of cutting, which arises from opposing rather than matching limbs; the phrase is circumstantial, describing them as cut in differing ways.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r5.anchor: و ( من ) لابتداء الغاية ؛ لأن القطع مبتدأ وناشيء من مخالفة العضو العضو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r6.claim: The phrasing “in the palm trunks” likens the crucified person’s firm placement to an object lodged in its container.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r6.anchor: شبه تمكن المصلوب في الجذع بتمكن الشيء الموعى في وعائه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r7.claim: “Which of us” refers to Pharaoh and Moses, as shown by Pharaoh’s claim that the converts believed Moses before Pharaoh gave permission.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r7.anchor: { أينا } يريد نفسه لعنه الله وموسى صلوات الله عليه بدليل قوله : { له قبل }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r8.claim: In Qurʾānic usage the lām with īmān can refer to belief in someone other than God, as at 9:61.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r8.anchor: واللام مع الإيمان في كتاب الله لغير الله تعالى ، كقوله تعالى : { يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين } ( التوبة : 61 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r9.claim: Pharaoh boasts of his power and familiar tortures, belittles and mocks Moses, and threatens him although Moses had never tortured anyone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p77#3/r9.anchor: وفيه نفاجة باقتداره وقهره ، وما ألفه وضري به : من تعذيب الناس بأنواع العذاب

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r8.claim: Pharaoh addresses the magicians: they affirmed Moses before Pharaoh ordered them to believe in him.
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r8.anchor: يعنى صدقتم لموسى { قبل أن ءاذن لكم } يقول: قبل أن آمركم بالإيمان لموسى

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r9.speaker: فرعون
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r9.claim: Pharaoh accuses Moses of being the magicians’ leader in magic and of teaching them.
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r9.anchor: فرعون: { آمنتم له } يعنى صدقتم لموسى { قبل أن ءاذن لكم } يقول: قبل أن آمركم بالإيمان لموسى { إنه لكبيركم }

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r10.claim: Cutting them crosswise means cutting the right hand and left foot.

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r11.claim: Here “in the trunks of the palms” means upon them, as in the cited wording from 52:38.
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r11.anchor: يعنى عليه { ولتعلمن أينآ أشد عذابا وأبقى } [آية: 71]

MUQATIL:20:69-71/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r12.claim: Pharaoh says they will learn whether he or the Lord of Moses and Aaron gives the harsher punishment.
MUQATIL:20:69-71/r12.anchor: أنا أو ورب موسى وهارون { وأبقى } وأدوم عذابا.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ reads without lengthening; Basran, Shāmī, and Ḥijāzī readers lengthen; others use two hamzas.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r1.anchor: بغير مد حفص وبهمزة ممدودة بصري وشامي وحجازي وبهمزتين غيرهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r2.claim: The pronoun refers to Moses; Arabic permits āmana lahu and āmana bihi.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r2.anchor: أي لموسى يقال آمن له وآمن به

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r3.claim: Kabīrukum means leader or teacher; Meccans call a teacher “my kabīr.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r3.anchor: لعظيمكم أو لمعلمكم تقول أهل مكة للمعلم أمرني كبيري

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r4.claim: Crosswise cutting severs the right hand and left foot; the phrase marks origin and describes the differing limbs.
