NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r4.anchor: القطع من خلاف ان تقطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى لان كل واحد من العضوين يخالف الآخر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r5.claim: Min marks the point of origin; the prepositional phrase is circumstantial accusative describing limbs made different.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r5.anchor: من لابتداء الغاية لان المقطع مبتدأ وناشئ من مخالفة العضو ومحل الجار والمجرور والنصب على الحال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r6.claim: The wording pictures the crucified person as contained in a trunk; palms are specified for their height.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r6.anchor: شبه تمكن المصلوب في الجذع بتمكن المظروف في الظرف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r7.claim: Pharaoh means he is harsher if they believe him or Moses' Lord is harsher if they reject Him; another view compares Pharaoh with Moses, since belief's lām in Quran is not used for God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p61#2/r7.anchor: انا على ايمانكم بي أو رب موسى على ترك الايمان به وقيل يريد بنفسه لعنه الله وموسى صلوات الله وسلامه عليه بدليل قوله آمنتم له واللام مع الإيمان في كتاب الله لغير الله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r23.claim: Āmantum lahu means that they believed in him; Arabic also uses āmana bihi, as in the verse about Lot.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:68-71/r23.anchor: قال آمنتم له } أي به يقال: آمن له وآمن به

QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r1.claim: The commentary cites the verse about Lot as an example of āmana lahu, believing in someone.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r2.claim: Pharaoh's question rebukes the magicians for transgressing and acting without his permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r2.anchor: إنكار منه عليهم أي تعديتم وفعلتم ما لم آمركم به

QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r3.claim: Pharaoh falsely called Moses their chief and teacher to confuse the people and prevent them from following the magicians' faith; Pharaoh knew they learned magic before Moses arrived or was born.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r3.anchor: وإنما أراد فرعون بقوله هذا ليشبه على الناس حتى لا يتبعوهم فيؤمنوا كإيمانهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r4.claim: Pharaoh threatens to cut off opposite hands and feet and crucify them on palm trunks.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r4.anchor: أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r5.claim: In the trunks means on the trunks; Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil's verse attests crucifixion on a palm trunk.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r5.anchor: هم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة فلا عطست شيبان إلا بأجدعا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r6.speaker: ابن محيصن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r6.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads both forms here and in al-Aʿraf with an open hamza and lighter consonant doubling, from the forms qataʿa and ṣalaba.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن هنا وفي الأعراف «فلأقطعن»، و«لأصلبنكم» بفتح الألف والتخفيف

QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r7.claim: By asking which gives harsher and more lasting punishment, Pharaoh means himself or the Lord of Moses.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r8.claim: The magicians were cut and crucified until they died; the author invokes mercy for them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:71/r8.anchor: فقطع وصلب حتى ماتوا رحمهم الله تعالى.

BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh rebukes the magicians for believing Moses without his leave.
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r1.anchor: {قال} فرعون للسحرة بطريق التوبيخ {له قبل} أي : لموسى

BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r2.claim: The lām in له incorporates the sense of following into the verb.
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r2.anchor: واللام لتضمين الفعل معنى الاتباع واللام مع الإيمان في كتاب الله

BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r3.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r3.claim: Al-Baḥr instead takes له to mean their Lord, with the lām functioning like bi; the parallel wording in al-Aʿrāf supports this reading.
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r3.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" : له أي : لربهما على أن اللام بمعنى الباء

BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r4.claim: The form read with a long vowel is declarative, expressing Pharaoh's reproach that they acted before he gave permission.
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r4.anchor: وآمنتم بالمد على الاخبار أي : فعلتم هذا الفعل توبيخا لهم

BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r5.claim: Before means they acted without his permission; it does not imply permission was later given or expected. Permission is informing someone that an action is approved.
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r5.anchor: من غير أن آذن لكم في الإيمان له وأمركم به

BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r6.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses the leading expert in their art and their teacher.
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r6.anchor: {إنه} يعني موسى {لكبيركم} أي : في فنكم وأعلمكم به

BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r7.claim: Kāshifī glosses Pharaoh's charge as calling Moses the magicians' master, teacher, and senior.
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r7.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يعني استاد ومعلم ومهتر جادوانست

BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r8.claim: Pharaoh fabricates a conspiracy to keep his people from following the magicians; he pretends faith requires his leave, so their unauthorized conversion is invalid, although he knows Moses did not teach them magic.
BURSEVI:v5p311#2/r8.anchor: وأراد التلبيس على قومه لئلا يتبعوا السحرة في الإيمان

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r1.claim: The threat implies an oath, and the intensive verb form signals repeated cutting; the same intensification applies to the following threat. Cutting can refer to perceptible bodies or intelligible things.
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r1.anchor: {فلاقطعن} أي : فوالله لأقطعن وصيغة التفعيل للتكثير

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r2.claim: Khilāf is broader than opposition: every pair of opposites differs, but not every pair that differs is opposite.
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r2.anchor: الخلاف أعم من الضد لأن كل ضدين مختلفان دون العكس

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r3.claim: The threat means cutting one limb from each side, such as the right hand and left foot; min marks the starting point from opposite rather than matching limbs, and the phrase describes their dissimilar state.
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r3.anchor: والمعنى من كل شق طرفا وهو أن يقطع اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r4.claim: The specific crosswise amputation makes the punishment more dreadful than other forms and strengthens the threat.
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r4.anchor: وتعيين القطع وكيفيته لكونه أفظع من غيره

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r5.claim: Crucifixion means fastening a person's back to wood, here palm trunks along the Nile.
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r5.anchor: الصلب الذي هو تعليق الإنسان للقتل قيل هو شد صلبه على خشب

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r6.claim: Using in with the palm trunks suggests the magicians will remain there a long time, like an object settled inside its container.
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r6.anchor: وإيثار كلمة في للدلالة على إبقائهم عليها زمانا طويلا

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r7.claim: A report says Pharaoh was the first to employ crucifixion.
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r7.anchor: قالوا : فرعون موسى هو أول من استعمل الصلب

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r8.claim: Though the recent miracle might make such threats seem implausible, Pharaoh may be deeply frightened yet feign toughness to maintain his public authority.
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r8.anchor: قلنا : يجوز أن يكون في أشد الخوف ويظهر الجلادة تمشية لناموسه

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r9.claim: Pharaoh means that the magicians will learn whether he or Moses is harsher and more enduring in punishment; Moses had inflicted no punishment, but Pharaoh thought they feared for their lives after seeing the staff swallow their tools.

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r10.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r10.claim: Under al-Baḥr's earlier reading of له as their Lord, the comparison is between Pharaoh himself and the Lord of Moses.
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r10.anchor: وعلى ما سبق من "بحر العلوم" في {له قبل}

BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r11.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p311#3/r11.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says Pharaoh speaks of severe punishment because he knows worldly pain but is blind to the severity of punishment in the afterlife.

NASHR:v1p368/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p368/r6.speaker: حفص ورويس والأصبهاني عن ورش
NASHR:v1p368/r6.claim: Hafs, Ruways, and al-Asbahani from Warsh read the three A-aamantum occurrences as declaratives.
NASHR:v1p368/r6.anchor: فقرأ الثلاثة بالإخبار: حفص ورويس والأصبهاني، عن ورش

NASHR:v1p368/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p368/r7.speaker: الخزاعي
NASHR:v1p368/r7.claim: Al-Khuzai alone reports this declarative reading through al-Shudha'i, al-Nahhas, and al-Azraq from Warsh, against the other Azraq routes.
NASHR:v1p368/r7.anchor: وانفرد بذلك الخزاعي، عن الشذائي، عن النخاس، عن الأزرق، عن ورش

NASHR:v1p368/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p368/r8.speaker: قنبل
NASHR:v1p368/r8.claim: For Taha, Ibn Mujahid reports Qunbul’s declarative reading, while Ibn Shanabudh reports the interrogative; the remaining readers use the interrogative.
NASHR:v1p368/r8.anchor: واختلف، عن قنبل في حرف طه، فرواه عنه بالإخبار ابن مجاهد، ورواه ابن شنبوذ بالاستفهام

NASHR:v1p368/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p368/r9.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف وأبو بكر وورش وهشام
NASHR:v1p368/r9.claim: These readers pronounce the second hamza fully in the A-aamantum form.
NASHR:v1p368/r9.anchor: وحقق في الثانية الثلاثة منهم حمزة والكسائي وخلف وأبو بكر ور وح

NASHR:v1p368/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p368/r10.speaker: هشام
NASHR:v1p368/r10.claim: Hisham’s route through al-Dajuni and al-Shudha'i reports full realization; al-Halwani and al-Dajuni through Zayd report an intermediate hamza.
NASHR:v1p368/r10.anchor: واختلف، عن هشام، فرواها عنه الداجوني من طريق الشذائي، ورواها عنه الحلواني والداجوني من طريق زيد بين بين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r1.claim: The lām with the verb “believe” in Qur’anic usage is used for a person other than God, as in believing God and believing the believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r1.anchor: واللام مع الإيمان في كتاب الله لغير الله كقوله يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r2.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari says the threat displays Pharaoh’s power and domination, his accustomed torture of people, and his belittling mockery of Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r2.anchor: وهو قول الطبري قال: يريد نفسه وموسى عليه السلام، والقول الأول أذهب مع مخرقة فرعون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r3.claim: The interrogative clause is suspended from لتعلمن and fills the two object slots, or one slot if the verb is construed like “know”; another parse makes أينا the object and treats the predicate as omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r3.anchor: ولتعلمن هنا معلق وأينا أشد جملة استفهامية من مبتدأ وخبر في موضع نصب لقوله ولتعلمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r4.claim: On another parse, أينا is a relative pronoun, with an omitted subject in its clause: “which of us is more severe in punishment and longer-lasting.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p358#2/r4.anchor: وأينا موصولة والجملة بعدها صلة والتقدير ولتعلمن من هو أشد عذابا وأبقى

RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r9.claim: The Qurʾān itself does not state that Pharaoh carried out his threat against the believing people, though reports establish that he did.
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r9.anchor: ليس في القرآن أن فرعون فعل بأولئك القوم المؤمنين ما أوعدهم به ولكن ثبت ذلك في الأخبار

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r2.claim: The nūn in the threats to cut off and crucify is an emphatic nūn functioning like an oath.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r2.anchor: والنون في: (لأقطعن) و(لأصلبن) نون التأكيد تجري مجرى القسم

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r4.claim: Pharaoh asks whether they believed in Moses before his permission; له means به, as in Lot believing in Abraham.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r4.anchor: آمنتم له أي: به، يعني لموسى كقوله: (فآمن له لوط)

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r5.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses their chief, teacher, and instructor in magic to persuade the crowd that their performance was collusion; he knew it was true and deliberately deceived them.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r5.anchor: يعني موسى لكبيركم أي: رئيسكم وأستاذكم ومعلمكم الذي علمكم السحر موهما بذلك للعوام

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r6.claim: Cutting crosswise means the right hand and left foot.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r6.anchor: يعني اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى، وقيل: أول من فعل ذلك وصلب هو فرعون

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r7.claim: One explanation takes the crucifixion to be on palm trunks; another treats the trunks as containers surrounding the victims.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r7.anchor: قيل: على جذوع النخل، قيل: تلك الجذوع لهم كالأوعية وهي الظرف

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r8.claim: Pharaoh asks whether his punishment or the Lord of Moses’ punishment is stronger for disobedience; the latter endures.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r8.anchor: على قولكم أنا أم رب موسى على معصيتكم إياه لو عصيتموه وأبقى أدوم

JISHUMI:v7p4701/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب، وابن إسحاق
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r9.claim: Abqā means more enduring punishment for disobedience and reward for obedience.
JISHUMI:v7p4701/r9.anchor: أبقى عقابا إن عصي، وثوابا إن أطيع، عن محمد بن كعب، وابن إسحاق

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r12.claim: Pharaoh’s charge that Moses was their teacher shows his failure to answer with proof, so he resorted to sophistry, threats, and deception.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r12.anchor: يدل قوله: (لكبيركم الذي علمكم) أنه عجز عن الحجة فعدل إلى الشبهة والوعيد والتمويه

THALABI:v6p252/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r19.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r19.claim: Pharaoh accuses Moses of being the magicians' chief and the teacher who taught them magic.
THALABI:v6p252/r19.anchor: إنه لكبيركم لرئيسكم ومعلمكم الذي علمكم السحر

THALABI:v6p252/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r20.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r20.claim: The punishment in which opposite limbs are cut off means the right hand and left foot.
THALABI:v6p252/r20.anchor: فلأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف يعني الرجل اليسرى واليد اليمنى

THALABI:v6p252/r21.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p252/r21.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p252/r21.claim: The phrase means on the trunks of the palm trees.
THALABI:v6p252/r21.anchor: ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل يعني جذوع النخل

BURHAN:v1p128/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p128/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p128/r3.claim: Zarkashi catalogs further differences between parallel passages: connective particles and forms such as after/from, to/for, and then/fa; this excerpt lists them without explaining each variation.
BURHAN:v1p128/r3.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى فى البقرة ﴿ وإذ قلنا ادخلوا هذه القرية فكلوا ﴾ بالفاء وفى الأعراف بالواو
